claim: Slugifying the title 'Crème Brûlée' gives 'cr-me-br-l-e', and 'Tom & Jerry' gives 'tom-jerry'.
why: The regex replaces every run of characters outside a-z and 0-9 with one hyphen, so each accented letter becomes a hyphen and does not vanish. The README says such characters are dropped, which would give 'crme-brle'. Both examples in the claim match what the code prints.

root.claim: Slugifying 'Crème Brûlée' gives 'cr-me-br-l-e' and 'Tom & Jerry' gives 'tom-jerry'.

atoms.evidence: slug.py replaces each run of non a-z0-9 characters with a hyphen, so è, û and é each become a hyphen; main.py prints 'cr-me-br-l-e'. The README's 'drops' is wrong.
The run ' & ' is one non-alphanumeric run and becomes a single hyphen; main.py prints 'tom-jerry'.
